setupSteps: Choose the bar load. Beginners start with an empty bar (about 20 kg for a standard Olympic bar, est.; check the bar label, because gym bars vary) or lighter; a fitness site advises starting with a bare bar before adding weight. Women's and training bars can be lighter (not researched).

Collars or clips on every set. Once there are plates on the bar, fit collars or spring clips on both ends and tug-test them. Plates can creep outward and one side can tip if the bar tilts; a Starting Strength article notes smooth sleeves make collars necessary. No row-specific rule was found, but the tilting risk applies. Load both sides evenly.

Bar start position. Two choices: (a) bar on the floor for every rep (a reset, like a Pendlay row or StrongLifts) or (b) bar held in the air for the set after taking it from the floor or from a low rack or safety stands. FitPlate beginner choice: start from the floor or from a low rack at about knee height (est.), because this lets you check the hinge before every set.
Foot position. Stand with feet about hip-width, the bar over the middle of your feet (about shin height, est.), toes slightly out, knees slightly bent.

Overhand grip (palms facing you when standing, backs of the hands forward): hands just wider than shoulder-width as the FitPlate default (est.). Some guides say shoulder-width, others wider; one pilot study (20 young men, bent-over row) found more lat activity at 150% of shoulder-bone width than 100%, while seated-row and prone-row studies favoured narrower grips, so this is not settled.

Underhand grip (palms facing up; Yates row variant): hands about shoulder-width. It uses the biceps more and makes a more upright torso natural, but it puts the biceps under stretch under load; Dorian Yates reported tearing a biceps on this lift and switched to overhand (secondary sources, weigh lightly). Beginners start overhand.
Thumbs wrapped, wrists straight, a full closed grip. Straps or lifting hooks are not needed for beginner loads.
Stand tall holding the bar, shoulders back and down, ribs down, belly braced.

Soft knees, then push the hips back (a hip hinge) until the torso tips forward to about 45 degrees above the floor (est.; guides range from about 30 to about 60 degrees). The spine stays long and flat (neutral): neither rounded nor over-arched.
Look at the floor about 1-2 m ahead so the neck stays in line with the spine.
Arms hang straight below the shoulders, bar just past the knees; this is the start position of every rep.
Spotter or staff: not needed for rows, but ask staff to watch the first session and check your back.

steps.title: Set your stance
steps.action: Feet hip-width, bar over mid-foot, knees slightly bent.
steps.feel: Weight spread through the whole foot.
steps.visualCheck: Side: bar above the middle of the foot; front: feet even.

steps.title: Hinge and take the grip
steps.action: Push your hips back, tip the torso forward with a flat back, and take the bar overhand just outside shoulder-width.
steps.feel: Stretch in the back of the thighs; no pinching in the lower back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: straight line from head to hips; torso about 45 degrees (est.); no rounding of the upper or lower back.

steps.title: Stand the bar up and re-set the hinge
steps.action: Lift the bar to hang below your shoulders, arms straight.
steps.feel: Legs and glutes hold the position; arms long.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and brace the belly.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the torso angle stays the same; elbows straight but not locked.

steps.title: Set the shoulder blades
steps.action: Draw the shoulder blades slightly back and down before the elbows bend.
steps.visualCheck: Side: shoulders not hunched toward the ears.

steps.title: Row: pull the elbows back
steps.action: Drive the elbows back and up, past the torso, pulling the bar toward the lower ribs or navel; the bar travels close to your thighs and body.
steps.feel: Squeeze across the middle of the back; biceps assist.
steps.visualCheck: Side: bar path in a near-vertical line to the lower ribs or navel; torso does not rise.

steps.title: Pause at the top
steps.action: Bar touches or nears the belly; hold with the torso still.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbows behind the torso line; hips and torso unchanged.

steps.title: Lower under control
steps.action: Let the bar descend along the same line until the arms are straight, shoulder blades relaxing last.
steps.visualCheck: Side: smooth path; no dropping; spine still flat.

steps.title: Finish the set and put the bar down
steps.action: After the last rep, bend the knees and hips and lower the bar to the floor or rack with a flat back; do not drop it.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back flat all the way down.

commonMistakes.title: Rounding the lower back
commonMistakes.text: Rounding the lower back. Why: the spine takes the bar's load in a weak position and the row becomes a lower-back exercise (several guides; one NASM blog notes the compressive load may not suit those with back pain). Fix: lighten the bar, practise the hinge with no load, check a side view, and switch to a chest-supported row if you cannot stay flat.

commonMistakes.title: Jerking or using momentum
commonMistakes.text: Jerking or using momentum. Why: heaving with the legs and torso hides weak muscles and loads the spine in uncontrolled ways. Fix: pause 1 second at the top, drop the weight, keep the torso still.

commonMistakes.title: Torso rising as you pull
commonMistakes.text: Torso rising as you pull. Why: shortens the range and moves work to the lower back and hips. Fix: hold the same torso angle; reduce the load; use the floor start for each rep.

commonMistakes.title: Bar drifting away from the body
commonMistakes.text: Bar drifting away from the body. Why: lengthens the lever and loads the lower back more. Fix: keep the bar close to the thighs and pull to the lower ribs or navel.

commonMistakes.title: Pulling to the chest with the shrug
commonMistakes.text: Pulling to the chest with the shrug. Why: the upper traps take over and the shoulder pinches. Fix: set the blades down first, elbows back, bar to the navel.

commonMistakes.title: Squatting the row
commonMistakes.text: Squatting the row. Why: dropping the hips in and out turns it into a swing. Fix: soft knees, fixed hips, hinge from the hips.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure briefly. Fix: breathe out on the pull, brace the belly without holding the breath.

commonMistakes.title: No collars or uneven plates
commonMistakes.text: No collars or uneven plates. Why: a plate can slide and tip the bar. Fix: collars and a tug-test every set.

commonMistakes.title: Going too heavy too soon
commonMistakes.text: Going too heavy too soon. Why: form breaks, spine risk. Fix: begin with an empty bar and add small amounts (see section 7).

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the bar from the top or letting the bar crash down
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the bar from the top or letting the bar crash down. Why: jolts the back and is unsafe for gym floors. Fix: lower under control; set it down with a flat back.

safetyNotes: Lower back: this is the main risk. If your lower back rounds, stop, lower the bar and lighten; if you cannot hold a flat back, use a chest-supported row. A NASM blog says the compressive load may not suit people with back pain or earlier injuries.
Biceps and elbows: the underhand row stretches the biceps under load; stop if you feel a sharp pain at the elbow or upper arm.
High blood pressure: avoid breath-holding and stop short of failure.
Spotter: not needed for rows, but ask staff to check your back in the first session and set safety stands at about knee height if racking the bar.
Equipment check: collars on every set, even plates, bar not bent, floor clear behind you.
Gym etiquette: do not drop the bar from height, strip your plates after use, wipe the bar, do not film other members, and ask staff before filming.

Note: all sources for this item were seen only as search-result summaries (pages not opened in full); many are coaching blogs. The elbow thresholds (150 and 90 degrees), the torso band (20-60 degrees, about 45 target), the 2.5 s minimum rep, the empty-bar start, plate steps and all sets, reps and rest values are FitPlate choices (est.), not validated. Not found: an ACE exercise library page for the barbell bent-over row; an NASM library page with steps; the ExRx standard bent-over row page; Harvard Health and Mayo Clinic pages on the barbell row; a professional-body row prescription; a Compendium code for vigorous resistance training (not opened); a validated torso-angle standard or a standard for the rounded-back threshold; peer-reviewed support for the Yates biceps-tear claim (anecdotal); condition-specific sources for knee pain, shoulder problems, obesity and PCOS; the primary ACOG page.
